title: BENCHMARKING SOCIOLINGUISTIC DIVERSITY IN SWAHILI NLP: A TAXONOMY-GUIDED APPROACH

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model prediction disparities using xAUC, Disparate Impact (DI), and Fairness Violation (FV) across different Kenyan tribal groups (e.g., Kikuyu and Kamba vs. others, Bantu vs. Non-Bantu), and using OLS regression to analyze how specific sociolinguistic features (Sheng, tribal lexicons, code-mixing, loanwords) correlate with model prediction errors.

Computing Disparate Impact (DI) and Fairness Violations (FV) across 1-way to 5-way combinations of binarized demographic attributes (age, gender, education, income, and tribal identity) to measure compounded performance disparities for marginalized subgroups.
